newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices closed Tuesday's post-holiday session flat to marginally higher as players awaited Wednesday's $189.8 million Florida Board of Education deal and a $271 million California Public Works offering.
Secondary activity was light following Monday's Presidents Day holiday, traders said.
"There's maybe just somewhat of a holiday-like atmosphere," one trader said, adding that some players decided to take Tuesday off as well.
A analyst said the municipal cash market overall ended unchanged to up 1/8 point. High-grade issues ended flat but with a firmer tone, while dollar bonds largely mimicked the broader market, he said.
Though most traders made similar assessments, one judged prices down 1/8 to 1/4 in spots.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 8/32 at 101 to yield 6.55 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed up 3/32 at 117-30/32.
The March T-bond contract closed down 3/32 at 113-27/32. The MOB spread was 131 ticks.

On the economic front, the market awaits Wednesday's release the January consumer price index. A survey of economists by Reuters found expectations for a 0.3 percent rise overall and a 0.2 percent increase in the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices.

As for new issues, Florida Board of Education is set to sell $189.84 million of general obligation bonds via competitive bidding at 1100 EST on Wednesday, according to the state Division of Bond Finance. Previously, the offering had been listed as day-to-day.
"I think it will be received well," a trader said, adding that anything that has a "decent story," and even things that do not, "are getting good numbers."
"They'll be well received, there's just not that many bonds around, and there's plenty of cash, and retail has been pretty good also," he said. "Definitely, we've got some real good inquiries here."
Florida's deal included, Wednesday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.3 billion in 33 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $940 million in 19 sales, with the $271 million California Public Works deal via Bear Stearns & Co topping the list.
On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $338 million are scheduled. Florida Board of Education's deal is the largest.
An additional five sales totaling $90 million are on the possible calendar, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds Wednesday depending on market conditions.
